doc:
ID: SAFFIRE-I
Name: Saffire-I Large-Scale Flame Spread over SIBAL Fabric
Program: Saffire | Platform: Cygnus OA-6 free-flyer (2016) | Hardware: Saffire Flow Unit, 46 cm duct
Verification: Verified against published paper
Fuel (solid): SIBAL cloth (75% cotton / 25% fiberglass), 41 cm x 94 cm
Conditions: O2=21%, pressure=100 kPa, airflow=20 cm/s, steady flame length=4 cm
Extinction/behavior: Flame reached a steady size instead of growing continuously as in normal gravity; burn lasted about 400 s
Sensors: Video cameras, thermocouples, radiometers, flame stand-off distance
Summary: First large-scale spacecraft fire test: concurrent and opposed flame spread over a thin charring fabric in a 20 cm/s airflow, away from the ISS.
Findings: Steady (not accelerating) concurrent flame spread over a large thin fuel in low gravity | Steady flame length about 4 cm, maximum about 6.2 cm (about 30% overshoot from boundary-layer development) | Average flame power about 1200 W (+/-300 W) per mission slides
Tests: I-1: SIBAL, O2=21%, 100 kPa, 20 cm/s, concurrent and opposed -> steady size 4 cm, max 6.2 cm
Fire-safety relevance: Validates models of realistic spacecraft fire growth for vehicle-scale scenarios. | Tags: habitat_flammability, predictive_modeling
Missing data: Spread-rate values are plotted in source figures; not yet extracted
Citation: Urban et al., ICES-2021-266, Table 2; Saffire I-III results slides (https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20210011521/downloads/ICES%202021-266%200503-2021%20final.pdf)

ID: SAFFIRE-II
Name: Saffire-II Oxygen Flammability Limits in Low Gravity
Program: Saffire | Platform: Cygnus free-flyer | Hardware: Saffire Flow Unit, 46 cm duct
Verification: Verified against published paper
Fuel (solid): SIBAL strips 5 cm wide x 30 cm, plus 5 cm wide two-sided PMMA (flat and grooved)
Conditions: O2=21%, pressure=100 kPa, airflow=20 cm/s, steady flame length=4 cm
Extinction/behavior: Narrow SIBAL samples burned to steady 4-5 cm flames; PMMA flames grew to 8.0 cm (grooved) and 9.5 cm (flat)
Sensors: Video cameras, thermocouples, radiometers
Summary: Multi-sample test to find the oxygen flammability limits of materials in long-duration low gravity; samples were placed with a long entrance length.
Findings: No flame-size overshoot on SIBAL when placed with a long entrance length | Average flame power about 200 W (+/-50 W) per mission slides | PMMA two-sided flames reached limiting lengths
Tests: II-5: SIBAL, O2=21%, 100 kPa, 20 cm/s, n/a -> steady size 4 cm; II-6: SIBAL, O2=21%, 100 kPa, 25 cm/s, n/a -> steady size 5 cm
Fire-safety relevance: Supports flammability limits for spacecraft materials. | Tags: habitat_flammability, ignition
Missing data: Conditions for the PMMA samples not extracted

ID: SAFFIRE-III
Name: Saffire-III Higher-Flow Repeat of Saffire-I
Program: Saffire | Platform: Cygnus free-flyer | Hardware: Saffire Flow Unit, 46 cm duct
Verification: Verified against published paper
Fuel (solid): SIBAL cloth, 41 cm x 94 cm (same as Saffire-I)
Conditions: O2=21%, pressure=100 kPa, airflow=25 cm/s, steady flame length=5 cm
Extinction/behavior: Steady flame size about 5 cm (max 8.2 cm); burn lasted about 320 s
Sensors: Video cameras, thermocouples, radiometers
Summary: Same material as Saffire-I at a faster airflow, to show how flow speed controls flame spread.
Findings: Flame speed is proportional to airflow velocity | Faster flow (25 vs 20 cm/s) gave a larger steady flame

doc:
ID: SAFFIRE-IV
Name: Saffire-IV Thin and Thick Fuels with Combustion-Product Monitoring
Program: Saffire | Platform: Cygnus NG-13 (ignited May 2020) | Hardware: Saffire Flow Unit (30 cm duct) plus Far Field Diagnostics
Verification: Verified against published paper
Fuel (solid): SIBAL cloth 50 cm; two-sided PMMA 18 cm x 1 cm thick
Conditions: O2=22%, pressure=100 kPa, airflow=20 cm/s, steady flame length=8.5 cm
Extinction/behavior: Thin SIBAL: steady flame 8.5 cm (max 11 cm). Two-sided PMMA stayed alight when flow stopped (bubbling fuel jets) and soot blocked the outlet screen
Sensors: Video (side and top cameras), thermocouples, radiometers, O2/CO2/CO gas sensors, aerosol monitors, remote CO2 and temperature sensors in six locations
Summary: Larger fires in a reduced-height duct, with measurement of heat, smoke and gases and a test of post-fire cleanup.
Findings: Reduced duct height roughly doubled SIBAL spread rate versus Saffire I and III | Two-sided PMMA flame persisted 15 s without flow; PMMA flame grew to 9.5 cm after 400 s | Deflagration seen at ignition on PMMA (stratified fuel vapor) | Heat release up to 10 kW; average vehicle conditions stayed acceptable (Saffire IV-V)
Tests: IV-1: SIBAL, O2=22%, 100 kPa, 20 cm/s, concurrent -> steady 8.5 cm, max 11 cm; IV-2: 2-sided PMMA, O2=22%, 100 kPa, 20 cm/s, concurrent -> grew to 9.5 cm in 400 s; delayed extinguishment; deflagration at ignition
Fire-safety relevance: Evidence for extinguishment strategy, smoke and gas products, and post-fire cleanup in a crewed vehicle. | Tags: habitat_flammability, extinguishment, smoke_detection, controls_equipment, ignition
Missing data: none
Citation: Urban et al., ICES-2021-266, Tables 1-2 (https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20210011521/downloads/ICES%202021-266%200503-2021%20final.pdf)

tests.result: grew to 9.5 cm in 400 s; delayed extinguishment; deflagration at ignition

doc:
ID: SAFFIRE-V
Name: Saffire-V Exploration Atmospheres (Low Pressure, Higher O2)
Program: Saffire | Platform: Cygnus NG-14 (January 2021) | Hardware: Saffire Flow Unit (30 cm duct) plus Far Field Diagnostics
Verification: Verified against published paper
Fuel (solid): Cotton jersey 50 cm; one-sided PMMA 18 cm x 0.5 cm; structured (ribbed) PMMA 20 cm x 1 cm
Conditions: O2=26.2%, pressure=70.7 kPa, airflow=20 cm/s, steady flame length=10 cm
Extinction/behavior: Reducing flow to 5 cm/s for 300 s before stopping it let PMMA flames extinguish immediately; thin cotton flame regrew when flow resumed after 70 s without flow
Sensors: Video, thermocouples, radiometers, O2/CO2/CO/HF/HCl sensors, aerosol monitors, remote CO2 sensors
Summary: Burned materials in reduced pressure and elevated oxygen (the kind of atmosphere planned for exploration habitats) and tested ways to promote extinguishment.
Findings: Thin fuel at higher O2 can keep burning without airflow | Reduced (not zero) airflow cooled the sample and gave faster extinction | Ribbed PMMA: flame speed depends on rib width (1-10 mm), not slab thickness | NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 does not capture low-gravity behavior of thick fuels
Tests: V-2: Cotton jersey, O2=26.2%, 70.7 kPa, 20 cm/s, concurrent -> steady 10.0 cm, max 14.0 cm; burned on after 70 s without flow; V-3: 1-sided PMMA, O2=25.4%, 71.3 kPa, 20 cm/s, concurrent -> grew to 11 cm in 450 s; extinguished right after 5 cm/s step-down; V-4: Structured PMMA, O2=25.7%, 72.6 kPa, 20 cm/s, opposed -> deflagration at ignition; faster spread on thin ribs
Fire-safety relevance: Closest available data to a low-pressure, oxygen-enriched Moon habitat; informs material screening standards and extinguishment strategy. | Tags: habitat_flammability, atmosphere_exploration, extinguishment, ignition, predictive_modeling
Missing data: none
Citation: Urban et al., ICES-2021-266, Tables 1-2 (https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20210011521/downloads/ICES%202021-266%200503-2021%20final.pdf)

deflagration at ignition; faster spread on thin ribs
